Here are five tips to build your first one: Pick one task you do repeatedly (tagging, routing, weekly recaps) Write clear instructions: the goal, the format, and what to do when it's unsure Add a trigger (on a schedule or when X happens) so it runs in the background Start with the minimum permissions it needs. Have you ever zoned out on a Zoom call, then realised you’ve missed the last two minutes? I’ve been trying Wispr Flow’s Notetaker, which records and transcribes meetings in real time. You can ask it what you missed, search previous meetings for specific decisions, and use the transcripts with tools like ChatGPT and Claude to draft follow-up emails or messages. Very useful if, like me, you spend a lot of time in meetings, and even more time trying to remember what actually happened in them.  It’s currently available on Mac and Windows, and the Notetaker is free to use. Copy the link for one month of Wispr Flow Pro for free: https://ref.wisprflow.ai/ali_tiktok_notetaker

People probably don’t want what you’re selling because they either think your product or service can help them solve their painful problem or they can’t afford it. If you’re trying to sell them the vehicle that helps them get to where they want to be, sometimes it’s really hard to get them to see the value, because they want a tangible outcome.

We've got a few hundred students in Lifestyle Business Academy now, all professionals starting their first online business. As you'd imagine, the outcomes are all over the place. Some of them are absolutely crushing it. Others have been with us for months and have barely got started. I've been thinking a lot about what actually separates the two. I reckon it comes down to three things. 1️⃣ First, the niche. Almost all of our most successful students picked something they already had skills or a network in. 2️⃣ Second, imperfect action. If you're struggling to figure out what to do with your life, try the Odyssey Plan. It's an exercise that Stanford Business School uses to help people figure out their path. You ask yourself three questions: 1️⃣ Your current path: If you continued down your current path, what would your life look like 5 years from now? 2️⃣ Your alternative path: If you had to take a completely different path, what would your life look like 5 years from now? 3️⃣ Your radical path: If you took a completely different path but didn't care what anyone thought and weren't worried about money, what would your life look like?
